text:
My neighbor recently decided to take security seriously, erecting a bold "Beware of Dog" sign that looked like it belonged on a fortress, not a suburban fence. The irony arrived the very next day when the postman knocked. Out trotted my three-pound furball, a creature whose primary defense mechanism is to look like a fluffy marshmallow that might blow away in a strong breeze.

The postman didn’t even flinch; he just smiled and said, "Oh no, I'm so scared!" It was the most sarcastic compliment I’ve ever received. But here’s the thing: my dog took that comment as a personal challenge. He’s now on a relentless mission to prove the postman wrong. He practices his "growl" (which sounds more like a squeaky toy being stepped on) and patrols the yard with the intensity of a tiny, furry bodyguard.

I’m starting to worry he’s going to try to intimidate a squirrel next. And honestly, if he can’t scare a postman, how is he supposed to handle the real threat: the color of an eggplant? Because let’s be real, that purple is the only thing that should be "beware" around here.
